Ethinyl estradiol and benzodiazepines: Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. Monitor closely. 2. Ethinyl estradiol and aminocaproic acid: Concomitant use may result in additive hypercoagulability. Estrogens increase clotting factor production and platelet aggregation, while aminocaproic acid inhibits fibrinolysis and plasminogen activity. Use caution and monitor. 3. Amoxicillin and ethinyl estradiol: Amoxicillin may reduce the levels or efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Ampicillin and ethinyl estradiol: Similar to amoxicillin, ampicillin may decrease the levels or efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Applies only to oral forms of the hormone. Low risk of contraceptive failure; use caution and monitor. 5. Artemether/lumefantrine and ethinyl estradiol: This combination may decrease the levels or efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 6. Atazanavir and norethindrone acetate: Atazanavir may decrease the effects of norethindrone acetate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Consider alternatives if available. 7. Ethinyl estradiol and atogepant: Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of atogepant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 8. Atorvastatin and ethinyl estradiol: Atorvastatin may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 9. Ethinyl estradiol and axitinib: Ethinyl estradiol may increase axitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 10. Ethinyl estradiol and bendamustine: Ethinyl estradiol may increase bendamustine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Bendamustine is minimally metabolized by CYP1A2, and ethinyl estradiol is a weak CYP1A2 inhibitor. Monitor plasma concentrations and use caution. 11. Ferrous fumarate and bictegravir: Ferrous fumarate may decrease bictegravir levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Bictegravir and iron-containing supplements can be taken together with food, but avoid simultaneous administration under fasting conditions. 12.
